scope: Executable compact target mappings, shared physical geometry and exact fractions, per-target metadata retention, compact section membership, and disjoint borrowing of operator VM workspaces. Wire format 40. Runs stay compact after decoding; no new playback cache or dependency.

method.device: ESP32 rev3.1, 240 MHz, one core, Wi-Fi off, GPIO untouched, standalone profiling image with 160 KiB heap. Same 32 timestamps, parameters and workloads as the baseline.
method.release: Optimization level 3, fat LTO, one codegen unit, panic=abort, debug=2 for attribution. Timed device images have per-instruction counters disabled.
method.equivalence: All 19 host workloads retain identical timestamps, active-effect counts, 608 frame CRCs and full instruction/pair/triple signatures. Program IDs are normalized because they follow allocation address order. The accepted complete device capture verifies all 544 frames, 17 cases and 16 profiling/control windows.
method.hotspots: Interrupted PCs at 997 and 1999 microseconds, bracketed by unsampled warm controls. Listed shares are self-symbol samples including inlined helpers, not isolated function timings. ROM/unresolved PCs remain explicitly unattributed.
method.heap: ESP32 decoded and retained values are allocator-used bytes. Retained includes decoded data, workspace and output buffers. Every measured device evaluation allocates zero times; workspace/output sizes remain unchanged.
method.host_peak: 64-bit host counting allocator, requested bytes excluding allocator metadata and stack. Decode/preparation peaks exclude the input archive. Input-plus-preparation peaks are derived sums of archive length and the measured preparation peak, not firmware upload high-water measurements. No laptop timing comparison.
method.capture: Accepted capture retains every declared PC sample. Failed serial captures were excluded rather than repaired. Final collector uses 4096-byte reads, a 100 ms timeout and a 64 KiB receive buffer.
method.limitations: Prepared evaluation and output-buffer encoding only, excluding network, storage, DMA and physical output. These short windows do not establish whole-show worst cases or confidence intervals. Dense starter and scheduled_1024 were not run on the device. No claim of improved cache hit rate or a general playback speedup.

regression_investigation.findings: Native inspection found duplicate pixel reconstruction for spatial contexts, six placeholder stores for nonspatial samples, and whole-VM move/default/drop work during recursive sampling. Current code reuses the pixel address, borrows a static unused context through an inlined wrapper, bypasses searching a single run, and lends disjoint VM workspace slices. No expanded tables were restored. These changes also affect native code layout; the remaining timing differences are not separately attributable to one operation or cache effect.
regression_investigation.remaining_tradeoff: Expanded direct record loads become compact address arithmetic and lookup. Final Stanford is 464 us slower, Shimmer1200 458 us slower, and Chase/Pulse16 792 us slower than baseline; FreezeFrame is 281 us faster. Simple black/sparse cases add 34-37 us. Smaller data has not produced a broad speedup, but retained heap falls substantially and nested workspace moves are removed.

native_scope: Xtensa entry operands from matching profiling ELFs, not maximum nested stack usage. Operator/effect run symbol sizes remain 18087/17822 bytes.

full_controller_build.configuration: release loader, dig-quad, built and linked but not flashed
